verdicts.strongest_argument: The hunter's own corroboration is the refutation. All three 8-Ks are indexed in filings.json with their item codes and exact acceptance stamps, and two of the three carry Item 7.01 - Regulation FD - which means Korn Ferry issued a press release on the signing (2026-06-29T10:10:16Z, items 1.01/3.02/7.01/9.01) and another on the completion (2026-09-01T20:38:21Z, items 2.01/3.02/7.01/9.01). This is a $4.35bn NYSE company (event.json) whose deal was publicly announced with a Reg FD release nine weeks before closing. And the tape marked it: the capture's last full bar is 84.65 on 2026-09-01, struck before the 20:38 UTC completion filing, against the baseline's 82.04 on 2026-09-08 - so -3.1% arrived in the three-and-a-bit sessions after the closing 8-K became public, against a 20-day realised vol of 21.9% (about 1.4% a day). That is better than two daily sigma of marking in exactly the window the information became available, which is the definition of already in the price. The second problem is the inference chain about consensus. event.json's fiscal_quarter_ending is Jul/2026 and the deal closed 2026-09-01 - after the quarter end - so a consensus containing no deal is not a market asleep, it is a sell-side correctly excluding a post-quarter event. That consensus of $1.35 is itself the exact midpoint of the $1.32-$1.38 diluted-EPS guide Korn Ferry published on 2026-06-23, which is verbatim in the captured social body at docs/f52fae6941a874956cc2c58ea2ab58deffdc2526.txt: 'Korn Ferry expects Q1 FY'27 fee revenue to range from $725 million to $745 million, with diluted earnings per share anticipated between $1.32 and $1.38.' The reported-quarter number is therefore a restatement of published guidance. Third, the 530k-share floor is an inference from a permissive instruction, not a fact: Item 3.02's 1% test is an exemption from reporting, and issuers routinely file the item voluntarily for below-threshold acquisition stock, so 'at least $44m of stock' is a lower bound the filing does not actually assert. What genuinely survives is narrower than the claim: the shape of the August-October guide, with first-time intangible amortisation and interest on the 2026-08-19 obligation, is not visible anywhere in this corpus - and I concede the capture cannot test whether it was published, because it ran zero web queries on this name.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every number in this claim is in captured wire copy, and the mechanism is contradicted by the baseline's own series. All three consensus-versus-actual pairs were published as real-time headlines and are quoted verbatim in docs/f52fae6941a874956cc2c58ea2ab58deffdc2526.txt: 'Korn Ferry reports Q1 adjusted EPS $1.31, consensus $1.24' (2025-09-09T10:55), 'Korn Ferry reports Q3 adjusted EPS $1.28, consensus $1.23' (2026-03-09T11:17), and for the June quarter the same document carries both the $1.38 expectation ('Wall St is expecting 1.38 EPS for $KFY Q4', 2026-06-16T12:00) and the $1.40 print (2026-06-23T22:03). The same document links the aggregation twice - estimize.com/intro/kfy?chart=historical&metric_name=eps is literally a published historical EPS-surprise chart for this ticker - so 'nobody sums the series' is not available here. Worse, the series is cherry-picked from a longer one in the same file, which also records 'Korn Ferry reports Q4 adjusted EPS $1.32, consensus $1.26' on 2025-06-18, a +4.8% beat that sits between the claimed +5.6% and breaks the 'halved twice' shape. And the causal step fails on the baseline's own numbers: the smallest beat in the hunter's series, +1.4% on 2026-06-23, produced the largest recent up-reaction at +5.83%, while the larger +4.1% beat on 2026-03-09 produced -1.53%. Within this sample beat magnitude and reaction are inversely related, so 'the up-reactions were earned in a fat-beat regime' is not what the data says - the June print was a thin beat with the corpus noting 'Quarterly Revenue Guidance Slightly Misses Expectations' (2026-06-23T12:46) and the stock rose almost 6% anyway. The observation that consensus sits exactly on the guide midpoint is also not evidence the market failed to mark the regime down; it is what a company that guides a quarter at a time produces mechanically.

interactions: Both findings ultimately lean on the same document for their key figure - docs/f52fae6941a874956cc2c58ea2ab58deffdc2526.txt is the only stored body in this capture, and it is where the $1.32-$1.38 guide (KFY#0's 'consensus contains no deal' premise) and all three beat-versus-consensus pairs (KFY#1) come from. The two claims also pull against each other: KFY#0 argues the market has not marked the stock for the deal while citing a -4.10% five-day drawdown as corroboration, and KFY#1 argues the stock sits near its 52-week high because nothing has been marked down. Both cannot be the right reading of the same run-in.
